media.transcription:
COUNTRY CLUB OF DETROIT. MINUTES OF MEETING OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS. HELD: OCTOBER 29, 1963.
[Page 265] GOLF, GROUNDS AND GREENS COMMITTEE

Mr. Barr announced the formation of a Committee consisting of Charles G. Chapman, Chairman, A. Fred Kammer, Jr., George Haggarty, Carlton M. Higbie, Jr., and Mrs. Harley G. Higbie, for the purpose of interviewing applicants for the position of Golf Professional left vacant by the death of Joe Belfore. The Committee will report its recommendations to the Board, however, selection of the new Golf Professional is to be made by the Board.

Mr. Higbie presented the letter of appreciation from Mrs. Belfore, and a general discussion was had regarding the handling of the Golf Shop and closing the Club accounts with the Estate of Joe Belfore. After discussion it was unanimously agreed that the Club would pay to Mrs. Belfore the sum of Seven hundred and fifty Dollars ($750.00) as a gift to her and to assist her in the settlement of obligations resulting from the long illness of her husband. On the recommendation of Mr. Higbie it was agreed that the Club would pay the sum of One thousand dollars ($1000.00) to Danny Bianco, Assistant Golf Professional, for services rendered during the past golfing season, and in addition, pay him Four hundred dollars ($400.00) for each of the months of January and February of 1964, and Two hundred dollars ($200.00) for the first half of March. Mr. Higbie stated that the Golf Shop would stay open for the Christmas Season and his recommendation that Mrs. Belfore be permitted to continue the Shop until January 2, 1964, was unanimously approved.

A discussion was had regarding the question whether and to what extent golfing privileges should be extended to David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore, sons of Joe Belfore.

On recommendation of Mr. Higbie, it was unanimously agreed that golfing privileges limited to them personally and not to guests or members of their respective families be granted to David and Jeffery Belfore, for a period of two (2) years from and after November 1, 1963. Both men shall have the right to sign chits for themselves and have the use of the Men's Grill and Locker Room.

people.story:
The 1963 Country Club of Detroit minutes name Joe Belfore's sons as "David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore", and grant both men two years of golfing privileges.[^ccd-minutes-1963]

Earlier research matched him to a death-index entry for a Joseph F. Belfore Jr., born August 21, 1917, who died in February 1982 in Fair Haven, Vermont.[^vt-jeffery] The match is tentative. A 1917 birth would mean his father was born by about 1897, which fits the family's other dates only if Joe was among the first children born in New Rochelle. The suggestion that his middle initial F. stands for Frank, after his uncle, is a guess with no source.

Update, November 2026. The Vermont record of a man born in 1917 is kept in his file, but it is probably someone else: Golfdom's note of a new baby for the Joe Belfores in 1941 and the 1950 census do not fit a man born in 1917.[^golfdom-1941-04][^census-1950-joe] Whether Jeffery is living is not known, so nothing more about him is added here.

people.summary: Sammy and Virginia's daughter, born in 1933. An English and theater teacher who married John Fleming and raised four children. She died in 2022 and is buried in Birmingham, Michigan.
people.story:
Patricia Hupp Belfore was born on June 11, 1933, the daughter of Sammy Belfore and Virginia Hupp. Her middle name came from her mother's family.[^patricia-findagrave]

In 1972 both of her father's obituaries listed her as Mrs. Patricia Fleming of Birmingham, Michigan.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Earlier research, based on her own obituary, records that she taught English and theater, that she married John Fleming in 1958, that they divorced in 1990, and that they had four children: Lisa, Chris, John and Geoff. The same obituary carries a family story that she was nearly cast as Bonnie Butler in Gone with the Wind.[^patricia-obit]

She died on January 1, 2022, aged eighty-eight, and is buried at Cedar Hill Cemetery in Birmingham, Michigan.[^patricia-findagrave] Where she died is less clear: this site's golfing page says Birmingham, while earlier versions of the tree placed her in Atlantis, Florida.

Sammy's New Rochelle obituary mentions three grandchildren, while Patricia had four children. One may have been born after 1972, or the count may simply be wrong.[^standard-star-obit]

Her funeral home obituary gives her birth as 6 August 1933 in Duluth, where her father spent his summers, and her death as 7 July 2022 in Atlantis, Florida. It says she was survived by her children Lisa, Chris, John and Geoff, four grandchildren, a son-in-law and a daughter-in-law.[^obit-patricia-fleming-2022-text]

He married Julia Clair. Volusia County property records show their Ormond Beach property passing to her trust in January 2025, which suggests he died in late 2024 or early 2025.[^volusia-2025]

people.summary: Giuseppe Circelli's father, a farm worker in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and the oldest Circelli yet found on this line. He died on 8 November 1839.
people.story:
Donato Circelli is the earliest name yet found on the Circelli side of the family. He was the son of Domenico Circelli and Annamaria Catalano, and he worked the land in San Bartolomeo in Galdo.[^death-donato-circelli-1839]

On 13 February 1827, aged forty-two, he registered the birth of his son Giuseppe, born the day before to his wife Vincenza; the family lived on Strada Borgo Nuovo.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827]

Donato died on 8 November 1839, aged forty-six, still married to Vincenza.[^death-donato-circelli-1839] His own father Domenico, then about eighty, died two months later, on 15 January 1840.[^death-domenico-circelli-1840] Ten years on, a copy of Donato's death act was filed with the papers for Giuseppe's wedding.[^processetti-circelli-mansolino-1850]

A Matteo Circelli, also "son of the late Donato", married in the same town in 1855, but his mother was Lucia Catalano. Because Donato was still married to Vincenza when he died, Matteo is more likely the son of another Donato Circelli; that link is not proven.[^matrimoni-1855-matteo-circelli]

people.summary: A Circelli of San Bartolomeo, son of a late Donato and Lucia Catalano. He is probably not Giuseppe's half-brother. Married Anna Palumbo in 1855.
people.story:
Matteo Circelli was twenty-one and a farmer when he married Anna Palumbo, eighteen, in San Bartolomeo on 7 January 1855. The act calls him the son of the late Donato and of Lucia Catalano, who was still living.[^matrimoni-1855-matteo-circelli] Their daughter Lucia was born a year later.[^nati-1856-circelli]

Giuseppe Circelli's father was also called Donato, so the two men were once thought to be half-brothers. The death records now argue against it. Giuseppe's father Donato died on 8 November 1839, still married to Giuseppe's mother Vincenza, who outlived him until 1843.[^death-donato-circelli-1839][^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843] Matteo was born about 1833, while that marriage was still going, to a different mother. So Matteo's father was most likely another Donato Circelli of the same town, and he is no longer linked to Giuseppe's family in the tree. Circelli was a common name in San Bartolomeo, and the two families may still have been cousins.

people.summary: The eldest known child of Giuseppe Circelli and Anna Rita Mansolino, born in January 1851. In 1884 she stood witness at the birth of her nephew Michael.
people.story:
On 18 January 1851 Giuseppe Circelli, a farm worker of twenty-four whose father Donato had died, came before the mayor of San Bartolomeo with a baby girl born to his wife Margarita Mansolino, twenty-three. They lived on strada Borgo. The girl was named Antonia.[^birth-antonia-circelli-1851] She was twelve years older than her sister Maria Donata.

She appears once more, as a grown woman. When her nephew Michael was registered on 17 December 1884, the first witness was "Circelli Antonia fu Giuseppe", thirty-three, a farm worker: the right name, the right father, already dead by then, and the right age.[^birth-michele-1884] Choosing her suggests the Circelli family stayed close to Maria Donata after she married Leonardantonio. Whom Antonia married, and whether she stayed in Italy, is not yet known. The town had several women named Antonia Circelli. The marriages of 1886 and 1890 that carry the name turned out to be weddings of their children, not hers.[^marriages-sbg-1886-1890-circelli]

people.summary: The youngest child of Mary and Joseph D'Onofrio (1934 to 2021). She grew up in Millburn, New Jersey, and raised six children.
people.story:
Dolores is the youngest of Mary and Joseph D'Onofrio's six children.[^donofrio-post-2010][^census-1940-donofrio] She was born in White Plains, New York, on 25 September 1934, and her obituary names her as the daughter of the late Joseph and Mary (nee Belfiore) D'Onofrio.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021]

She settled in Millburn, New Jersey, the town where her father had worked at his brother Frank's nursery, and graduated from Millburn High School in 1952. She was a homemaker and later worked for the Millburn Township Police Department. She loved feeding her large family, and Sunday gravy dinners brought everyone together; when they were all gathered she would say, "Look at what I made!" She was a movie buff and a sports fan.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021]

She raised six children, and she left nineteen grandchildren and four great-grandchildren when she died on 15 November 2021. Her brother Raymond's 2002 obituary lists her as his sister, Deloris Saggio.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021][^obit-index-raymond-donofrio-2002]

people.summary: He and Annie Hussey raised Dorothy. The censuses list her as their granddaughter, so he is probably Seb's great-great-grandfather, not her father.
people.story:
Family story, and the census, say that Patrick and his second wife Annie raised Dorothy, Seb's grandmother, after Dorothy's mother died young. The 1930 and 1940 censuses list Dorothy as their granddaughter. They also give her parents' birthplaces as New York. Patrick himself was born in Ireland, so he is not her father on those records. Later obituaries of Annie's children name Dorothy as a sister; that family language is kept beside the census, not in place of it.[^family-knowledge][^hennessy-census-1930-image][^hennessy-census-1940-image][^obit-patricia-dillon-2021][^obit-francis-hennessy-2013][^obit-anne-latino-2024]

Update, November 2026. Patrick was very probably the child baptised on 12 April 1874 at Conahy, County Kilkenny, son of Patrick Hennessy and Kate Brennan. Those are the parents named when he married Anna Marie Hussey on 17 June 1914.[^hennessy-baptism-1874][^hennessy-marriage-1914]

He arrived in New York on 11 January 1894. He declared his intention on 15 September 1905 and was naturalized on 18 October 1905. No passenger list for that January day has been found.[^hennessy-naturalization-1905]

His first wife was Mary, surname not yet known. She is with him in 1905, and by 1910 he was a widower at Premium Point. Their sons were Joseph, Thomas, Henry, and John, called Jack.[^hennessy-census-1905][^hennessy-census-1910][^hennessy-census-1915]

In 1910 his work was with the horses at Premium Point. In 1920 he owned 101 Huguenot Street, a chauffeur for a private family, and he told the census taker that his native tongue was Irish. In 1925 he lived at number 260, in the house of his employer Sidney Williams. In 1930 he and Annie were at 3 Fair Oaks, Premium Point, and in 1940 they were still on Premium Point.[^hennessy-census-1910][^hennessy-census-1920][^hennessy-census-1925][^hennessy-census-1930][^hennessy-census-1940]

A draft card for a Patrick Joseph Hennessy of Huguenot Street gives a birthday of 18 April 1877. That date does not fit the baptism, so the card has been kept as another reading, not as his birthday. A New York State death index entry for Patrick J. Hennessy, died 27 June 1947 at New Rochelle, aged 70, certificate 38983, is probably his. Aged 70 that June fits a birth in 1876 or 1877, which agrees with the draft card and not with the 1874 baptism. Both dates are kept until the death certificate, or another record, settles the year.[^hennessy-wwi-draft][^nys-death-index-1947-hennessy]

Update, November 2026. Annie was Anna Marie Hussey, born in New York about 1886 or 1887, daughter of James Hussey and Marie Dunn, both born in Ireland. In 1900 she was on Dean Street in Mamaroneck with her mother Maria and her brothers and sisters Theodore, Mary Ellen, Lizzie (indexed as Sizzie), and Frank. In 1910 she was a bookkeeper in a grocery on Cleveland Avenue in New Rochelle, in her sister's Chapman household, and an aunt, Annie Dunne, was in the house. She married Patrick on 17 June 1914.[^hussey-census-1900][^hussey-census-1910][^hennessy-marriage-1914]

Family story, and the census, say that Annie and Patrick raised Dorothy after Dorothy's mother died young. The 1930 and 1940 censuses list Dorothy as their granddaughter, not their daughter. Later obituaries of Annie's own children name Dorothy as a sister; that family language is kept beside the census.[^family-knowledge][^hennessy-census-1930-image][^hennessy-census-1940-image][^obit-patricia-dillon-2021][^obit-francis-hennessy-2013][^obit-anne-latino-2024]

people.story:
Francesco Mansolino was a farm worker in San Bartolomeo in Galdo. On 20 February 1829, aged thirty-five, he went to the town hall to register the birth of his daughter Anna Rita, born that morning to his wife Brigida. He was still living in January 1850, when Anna Rita married Giuseppe Circelli and the act named him as her father, a contadino, without the word "late".[^marriage-circelli-mansolino-1850]
